sentences.text: In respect of an accident which occurred on 16.01.2012, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.2,56,240/- to Kadegowda, the appellant in M.F.A. NC: 2024:KHC:50718 No.4197/2018 and a sum of Rs.4,53,000/- to the appellant in M.F.A. No.4199/2018.
2. Being dissatisfied with the award of compensation, both the claimants are in the appeals seeking enhancement.
3. In respect of the claimant - Kadegowda, the Tribunal has accepted the assessment of whole body disability at 12%, as stated by the doctor.

In my view, the assessment of whole body disability at 12%
is just and proper.

4. The Tribunal has taken the notional income of the claimant as Rs.6,000/-, since there was no Sri.Kadegowda vs M/S The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171689448/
3 evidence to that effect.

sentences.text: As the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority has determined the notional income as Rs.7,000/- for the accident of the year 2012, it would be appropriate to determine the notional income of the claimant at Rs.7,000/-.

Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,61,280/- (Rs.7,000/- X 12 X '16' X 12%) towards 'loss of future earnings'.
6.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.60,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' and Rs.40,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.
In my view, it would be appropriate to enhance the said sum to Rs.70,000/- and Rs.50,000/- respectively.
7. The Tribunal has not awarded any sum towards 'medical expenses', since no bills were produced.

However, since the evidence indicates that he was hospitalized in Victoria Hospita for about 10 days,
it would be appropriate to award Rs.10,000/- under the said head.
8. The Tribunal has taken the laid-up period as three months.
In my view, since the income is now taken as Rs.7,000/-, it would be appropriate to award NC: 2024:KHC:50718 Rs.21,000/- towards 'loss of income during laid-up period'.
9. The Tribunal has not awarded any sum towards 'conveyance, food, nutrition and attendant charges'.
Since the claimant was hospitalsed for 10 days, it would be appropriate to award Rs.15,000/- under the said head.

10. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:

Accordingly, the appellant - claimant in M.F.A. No.4197/2018 is held entitled for compensation of Rs.3,27,280/- as against Rs.2,56,240/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realisation.
12. In respect of the appellant - claimant in M.F.A. No.4199/2018, the Tribunal has assessed the whole body disability at 25%.
In my view, it is just and proper since the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 62% to the particular limb.
13. The Tribunal has taken the notional income of the claimant as Rs.6,000/-, since there was no evidence to that effect.

As the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority has determined the notional income as Rs.7,000/- for the accident of the year 2012, it would NC: 2024:KHC:50718 be appropriate to determine the notional income of the claimant at Rs.7,000/-.

14. Since the claimant was aged 31 years and the disability suffered is at 25%, 40% is to be added towards future prospects to determine monthly income of the claimant for awarding compensation towards 'loss of future income' which comes to Rs.9,800/-.
15. Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.3,59,800/- (Rs.9,800/- X 12 X '17' X 25%) towards 'loss of future earnings'.
16. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.70,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' and Rs.40,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.

In my view, it would be appropriate to award Rs.80,000/- and Rs.60,000/-
respectively under the said heads.
17. It is noticed that the claimant was hospitalized for about 30 days at Victoria Hospital.
In my view, even NC: 2024:KHC:50718 though no medical expenses is awarded, it would be appropriate to award Rs.15,000/- towards 'medical expenses', in view of the length of the stay in the hospital.
18. The Tribunal has taken the laid-up period as six months.

Since the income is taken at Rs.7,000/-, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.42,000/- (Rs.7,000/- X 6 months)
towards loss of earnings during laid up period.

19. The Tribunal has not awarded towards 'conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges,
since the claimant was hospitalized for over 30 days, it would be appropriate to award Rs.30,000/-
under the said head.
